notes: AMBIGUOUS 6-digit date, confirmed by owner as DDMMYY (not YYMMDD). Dot-matrix ink on a shiny metal tin lid - low contrast, strong reflection. 'KJ234' batch code on the same line must not be read as a date.

DD MM YY, space separated. The 'M6EXPM' machine code runs straight into the EXP label with no gap, and a vertical '21:35' TIME is printed alongside, rotated 90 degrees. Glossy foil packet, blurred. Malay product (PERISA PEDAS).

TWO dates: PRD DATE:23/06/2026 printed directly above - parser must pick EXP, not PRD. Bilingual header 'BEST BEFORE / BAIK SEBELUM (DAY/MONTH/YEAR)' confirms DD/MM/YYYY. Batch 42601965-2306AP6B and time 18:22 also present. Creased label.

Korean skincare. YYYY.MM.DD printed as 'EXP 2028.06.02까지' - the Hangul suffix means 'until' and must be stripped. 'LOT.5F0301' above could be misparsed as a date. Curved cap, dot-matrix on speckled surface. Good PAO candidate.

MANUFACTURE DATE ONLY - no expiry printed anywhere on the product (confirmed by owner). The parser must classify this as manufacture and NOT return it as an expiry, otherwise the app tells the user the item expired in May 2026. Correct behaviour is to ask the user or apply a category shelf life. Month-only MFG resolves to the FIRST of the month (conservative: any derived expiry lands earlier). '10:39' time and '041' line code on the same line are distractors.

Genuine NPRA-registered Malaysian medicine (MAL19950914T, Teck Aun Medical Factory, Eagle & Pagoda Brand). MM/YY on a gold-foil band around a small wrapped stick - curved, reflective. Batch code CK221281 sits directly beside the date on the same line and must not be absorbed into it. Verified end to end: real PaddleOCR reads 'CK221281 EXP:12/28' and the parser returns 2028-12-31 with high confidence, no review needed.

Toothpaste tube (Haleon group, made in Malaysia). Date is embossed at the crimp with a printed '/' between month and year, no ink - physically present but essentially invisible to a camera. No EXP keyword anywhere; the crimp position is the only convention marking it as the expiry, same as most tube packaging. The date_text above is the ground truth confirmed against the physical tube, and the parser correctly resolves parse('03/2027') to 2027-03-31 when given that clean string - see test_date_parser.py.
known_ocr_gap: Real PaddleOCR (both tiers) fails to read the embossed month digit and returns only the year fragment ('2027' amid unrelated garbled text). This is a genuine, currently-unsolved limitation of the OCR layer on no-ink embossed text, not a parser bug - kept as documented evidence rather than excluded, and xfailed (not skipped) in test_ocr.py so it surfaces the moment OCR improves enough to read it.
